#9144. Does Creatine Increase DHT? What You Need to Know

Ah, creatine! It’s a popular supplement promising muscle gains and enhanced performance. But as you’re hitting the gym harder and seeing results, there are some potential side effects to be aware of. Here’s the lowdown.

Creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle cells. It helps to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP) — your muscles’ go-to fuel when working hard.

Although you can find creatine in foods like red meat and seafood, many gym enthusiasts and athletes boost their stores with supplements. Why? Because more creatine equals more ATP, which means more energy for high-intensity activities. More fuel means more mileage!

Now, here’s where things get hairy. You might dial up your body’s DHT (dihydrotestosterone) production when you uplevel creatine. DHT is a derivative of testosterone and plays a big-league role in developing male characteristics. But here’s the catch: while DHT might beef up your alpha vibe, it’s also notorious for thinning out hairlines in peeps predisposed to male pattern baldness.

So, do creatine supplements cause baldness? Maybe! The buzz mainly stems from a small 2009 study where college-aged rugby players loaded up on creatine and saw their DHT levels increase significantly.

Because DHT can shrink hair follicles and shorten the hair growth cycle, it may seem logical to blame creatine for contributing to hair thinning. However, it’s important to remember that these findings are a one-hit wonder — they haven’t been seen again in other studies. Plus, let’s not forget that intense workouts alone can pump up these hormones, too.

As a result, the jury’s still out, making the creatine-and-baldness saga a hot topic for gym gossip and scientists alike.

The same 2009 study found that after a week of taking high-dose creatinine at 25 grams per day, DHT levels rose by 56%. When the researchers dropped the dose to 5g daily for two more weeks, levels remained 40% higher than baseline. These findings contrasted with the control group participants who took a placebo.

Does this mean creatine could spell disaster for your do? Well, creatine boosts DHT, the usual suspect in male pattern baldness, also called androgenic alopecia. However, your disposition to hair loss and the effects of DHT is genetic, meaning that it’s inherited.

Some folks are more prone to DHT’s hair-ruffling effects because of how their androgen receptor gene is wired. Hormones like testosterone and DHT bind to androgen receptors, typically triggering normal hair growth. However, variations in the AR gene make the androgens extra effective, making you more likely to experience hair loss.

So, while there isn’t much evidence to say that creatine supplements cause hair loss, the connection to increased DHT levels is worth considering if your family reunions look like a convention for bald eagles.

Beyond the potential for a breezy scalp, creatine is actually solid in the safety department, with long-term studies giving it a thumbs up. However, although creatinine doesn’t pose a risk to healthy individuals, it might not be your best move if you have kidney, high blood pressure, or liver disease.

Another thing to keep in mind is that creatinine loves to hang onto water, so expect some extra bloat and weigh-in surprises as your body adjusts.

Thinking of starting a creatine kick? Chatting with your doctor first is always wise, especially if you have other health conditions or take medications. They can advise you and rule out any potential interactions.

If you’re taking creatinine and notice changes to your hair, a check-up is a good idea. Shedding a few strands is normal, but it’s a red flag if you start losing clumps of hair. Rapid hair loss can indicate underlying health issues that go beyond your hairstyle.

Furthermore, consult a doctor if hair loss is weighing on your mind. They can offer solutions or treatments to manage your hair loss and stress.

Creatine is celebrated for its muscle-building prowess, but rumors of a link with hair loss exist. The good news is there’s little conclusive evidence directly connecting creatine supplementation to permanent hair loss.

However, creatine loading may boost DHT levels, a hormone linked to male pattern baldness, especially in people genetically predisposed to hair thinning.

So, if you’re concerned about hair loss, it might be wise to talk with a doctor before adding creatine supplements to your muscle-building routine.

AI video generation has matured at an astonishing speed. One minute people were mocking attempts to generate footage of Will Smith eating spaghetti, the next we have tools capable of generating footage for everything from photorealistic commercials and animated explainers to social media ads and cinematic short films, all based on simple text prompts.

But choosing the best AI video generator for you isn't only a question of visual quality. The increasing number of models available have varying limitations and strengths and weaknesses in different areas. Pricing structures can also vary wildly, and subscription fees often represent only a fraction of the cost.

Many AI video generators operate on credit systems, charge extra for premium models, or limit video length and resolution in ways that can quickly inflate your spend. With that in mind, here we take a deeper dive into the five best AI video generators available today, which we've ranked according to overall value as well as their flexibility and practical usefulness for professional creatives.

Whichever model or models you choose to work with, you'll probably want one of the best laptops for video editing or the best desktop PCs for video editors.

Adobe is already a powerhouse in filmmaking thanks to Premiere, which we rate as the best video editing software. As a result, Firefly more than just an AI video generator. Unlike many rivals that function as standalone tools, it integrates into Premiere and the wider Creative Cloud environment, making it significantly easier to incorporate AI-generated footage into existing professional workflows.

The most recent video-generation capabilities are particularly impressive. Prompt adherence is strong, footage tends to look polished and cinematic, and Adobe has invested heavily in making outputs commercially viable for professional users.

As announced at Adobe Max 2026, the native Firefly Video editor has been expanded to make it easier to combine clips with other elements such as images and sound effects, and projects created in Firefly Boards, Adobe's collaborative brainstorming space, can be carried straight into the video editor. There's also Adobe's AI agent, which makes using its software more intuitive and conversational.

Sign up to Creative Bloq's daily newsletter, which brings you the latest news and inspiration from the worlds of art, design and technology.

The Adobe name also offers reassurance in terms of safety and reliability. The platform's unlikely to disappear or radically change from one day to the next, and output from the native Firefly Video Models is intended to be safer for commercial use since they were trained on licensed material rather than scaped copyrighted video.

On the other hand, if you do want to use other models, they're here in Firefly itself. Google Veo, Kling, Runway and Luma AI's Ray are all integrated and ready to use in Adobe's platform, so you get not only the top AI video generator on our list but access to the second, third and fourth too!

Pricing: Adobe's Firefly Standard plan costs $9.99 per month and includes 2,000 generative credits, enough for around twenty 5-second AI video clips at 1080p quality. Higher-tier plans increase those allowances. Adobe currently prices 1080p video generation at roughly 100 credits per second, meaning a single 5-second clip consumes around 500 credits.

You can also access Firefly video generation through a Creative Cloud Pro plan, which gives you access to Adobe's suite of apps, including Premiere and Photoshop. Just note that you may need to pay for additional generative credits depending on how much footage you're generating, and partner models have different credit costs.

If pure visual quality is your priority, Google Veo has a strong claim to being the most impressive video model currently available. The platform is particularly good at realistic movement, lighting, camera behaviour and environmental detail.

Veo's ability to generate convincing cinematic scenes has made it popular among advertisers, content creators and filmmakers seeking premium-looking footage without a full production budget.

Pricing: Google offers Veo through consumer subscriptions and API access. For developers, Veo 3.1 costs roughly $0.40 per generated second, putting a typical 5-second clip at around $2.00 before retakes. That's easily the most expensive platform in this comparison, but it also delivers some of the highest-quality output available.

You can also access Veo through Google Gemini, Google AI Studio and through Adobe Firefly (see above). Through Gemini, there is a free tier offering just 3 video generations a day, at the time of writing, Google AI Pro costs $19.99 a month for 1,000 Flow credits, which translates to around 100 Lite videos or 10 high-quality Standard videos at 720p with a watermark. Google Ultra AI takes at $99.99 a month and upwards gives you 25,000 credits a month, enough to generate thousands of draft clips at 1080p.

Runway remains one of the most mature AI video platforms on the market. While some competitors may occasionally produce more realistic footage, Runway excels at putting creators in control. The platform includes advanced camera controls, editing features and creative tools that make it particularly appealing to professionals who want more than simple text-to-video generation.

The video editing features enable you to do things such as isolate a subject and remove the background, colour grading, adjusting the depth of field, making a slow motion version of your footage, and 'Inpainting', which means you can easily remove unwanted objects.

Pricing: Runway has several subscription tiers, ranging from entry-level plans through to professional and enterprise options. The credit-based system rewards efficient users but can become costly during experimentation. The Standard plan starts at $15 per month and includes 625 credits. According to Runway's published figures, that's enough for around 52 seconds of Gen-4.5 video generation. A creator producing multiple social videos every week will likely need the Pro plan at $35 per month or higher.

The Chinese platform Kling has become one of the biggest disruptors in AI video generation. It consistently produces impressive results while undercutting many western competitors on price.

Human movement, character animation and stylised content are particular strengths. For YouTubers, social creators and small businesses, Kling often represents the best balance between quality and affordability.

Pricing: Paid plans start at under $10 per month, and a 5-second 1080p clip generally consumes around 40 credits. That works out to roughly $0.40-$0.60 per clip depending on subscription tier, making Kling one of the most cost-effective premium AI video generators currently available and generally cheaper than Veo and Runway. However, as with most platforms, higher-quality generations consume credits faster.

Not every project needs blockbuster-quality visuals. Sometimes speed matters more than perfection, and that's where Hailuo shines. The platform is built around rapid iteration, allowing creators to test ideas quickly and cheaply. Agencies often use it during concept development before moving final production to more advanced systems.

Pricing: Hailuo is typically among the most affordable options available. Standard plans start between $8 and $15 per month depending on promotions and region. A typical 1080p generation consumes about 50 credits, placing the cost per clip around $0.50-$0.75.

The main trade-off is quality, and you might find yourself generating more clips to achieve a satisfactory result, which can offset the initial cost advantage. Additional editing and post-production work may also be required.

Before diving in to AI video generation, it's worth remembering that subscriptions don't always tell the whole story. A $10-per-month plan may sound inexpensive, but the number of usable clips you can generate could be surprisingly limited.

Making direct comparisons between AI video generators is difficult because some services charge per second of output, while others use credit systems that effectively works out as a cost per clip.

Pricing can also vary depending on which plan you choose and how much you use it. Heavy users are likely to have to pay extra for more credits, and plans are continually in flux. Providers have been making regular changes to their pricing as new models roll out and the competitive landscape changes. The prices being quoted today could easily change in a few weeks' time.

The challenge with any AI video generation is that creating a complete project often requires multiple generations. A single eight-second clip may be excellent, but producing several matching shots for a finished sequence can dramatically increase usage costs. You'll often need to generate dozens of variations before selecting a final clip, turning what appeared to be a modest monthly subscription into a much larger operational cost.

Users will also usually need separate editing software to assemble final productions.

For most creative professionals, we think Adobe Firefly currently represents the most balanced and versatile package while also offering reasonable value. While Google Veo may edge ahead on raw visual realism and Runway offers deeper creative controls, Firefly's integration with professional creative software makes it the most practical choice for real-world production environments, and Firefly does also provide access to Veo and Runway too.

That said, the right tool depends heavily on your needs. Consider Veo for cinematic quality, Runway for directorial control, Kling for affordability and Hailuo for rapid experimentation. Just don't judge any platform by its headline subscription price. In the AI video market, credits, render limits, premium models and editing requirements often matter far more than the monthly fee itself.

I sit down with Hailin Jin, Adobe's research lead for imaging and design, to discuss how the project could revolutionise vector design.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sneaks is often the highlight of Adobe MAX, giving the brand an opportunity to share the exciting innovations it's working on. Among the wild Adobe Sneaks announced today, one tool in particular could be game-changing for a whole host of creatives, from illustrators to concept artists, marking an exciting upcoming era for the brand.

Project Link Up is set to revolutionise vector design, turning the simple dragging function into context-aware fusion that automatically matches a scene's perspective. (TLDR: constantly redrawing objects at new viewing angles could soon be a thing of the past).

To understand more about Project Link Up, I caught up with Hailin Jin, senior principal scientist and research lead for imaging and design at Adobe, to get his behind-the-scenes insight into the work.

Mohit and the team started with an observation about an everyday gesture: dragging an object. Design tools usually interpret that as an instruction about placement, but there’s much more intent in what a designer moves, where they move it and how they move it.Placing an illustrated car into a parking space, for example, can involve separately adjusting its perspective, scale and style. The team asked whether the gesture itself could communicate more of that creative direction and help adapt the object to its surroundings, while keeping the result editable.

Yes. In our current prototype, a creativity slider lets the designer guide how subtle or expressive the adaptation should be, from preserving more of the original form to exploring a more dramatic transformation.The goal is to combine the ease of a gesture with explicit creative control. The resulting vector artwork remains editable, so designers can continue refining it.

Two contrasting styles don’t necessarily need to become one. The key is understanding the creator’s intent: should the object match the scene, retain its own personality, or create a deliberate contrast?Project Link Up explores combining the drag gesture and scene context with creative controls and prompt guidance. A designer could specify “match the scene’s illustration style” or “keep this character’s style, but adapt its perspective and lighting.”The aim is to help designers steer the relationship between elements, while keeping the resulting vector artwork editable.

The philosophy is to make creative exploration more immediate. When combining two elements requires substantial adjustment before you can judge whether an idea works, that effort can interrupt the process of discovery.Link Up explores how a familiar gesture could let designers try different relationships between objects, see what happens and develop the ideas they find interesting. Keeping the result editable as vector artwork matters: a promising combination becomes something the designer can continue shaping.

A strong example is manually reworking an asset to fit a new scene, particularly redrawing it from a different perspective. The team is exploring how that adaptation could happen as the designer places the object. That could reduce the preparation needed to evaluate a composition and give designers more time to refine the creative decisions that make it work.

A major direction in our research is helping tools understand creative content and the relationships within it. That understanding can make interactions more meaningful: moving an object into a scene could communicate an intention about perspective or composition, rather than simply a new position.For experienced designers, the opportunity is to express their judgment more directly and retain precise control over the result. Link Up explores one part of that future. We want to learn what creators expect a gesture to mean and how tools can respond in ways that feel useful and predictable.

#9141. 10 Signs You Might Not Really Be in Love: How to Tell the Difference

Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

Wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

Feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:

Caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

Chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner plans suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future plans feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

If imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love plans a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

Remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

Feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

No respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

If they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

If your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

True love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

Are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.

Last medically reviewed on June 26, 2024

Most estate planning advice assumes you will work until 60-65, accumulate wealth gradually, and have employer-provided benefits until Medicare kicks in. The FIRE path breaks every one of those assumptions. You may stop working at 35, 40, or 50 — meaning your estate plan must cover a potentially 40 to 50-year retirement, not the 20 to 25-year retirement conventional planning addresses.

This extended timeline creates unique vulnerabilities:

The SECURE Act fundamentally changed how inherited retirement accounts work, and this change matters enormously for FIRE households that have built large tax-advantaged portfolios.

Before the SECURE Act, non-spouse beneficiaries could "stretch" inherited IRA distributions over their own lifetime, allowing decades of tax-deferred growth. Now, most non-spouse beneficiaries must withdraw the entire inherited IRA balance within 10 years of the original owner's death. For a beneficiary in their peak earning years, this compressed timeline can push them into the 32% or 37% tax bracket on every distribution.

The FIRE advantage: Early retirees have years — sometimes decades — of lower taxable income between leaving work and taking Social Security or required minimum distributions. This creates a golden window for Roth conversions that no conventional retiree has.

A married couple who retires at 40 with $1.5 million in a traditional 401(k) and a $500,000 Roth IRA could systematically convert $80,000 to $100,000 per year from the traditional to the Roth, staying within the 22% bracket. Over 15 years, they convert $1.2 million to $1.5 million at a known, relatively low tax rate. Their heirs then inherit a Roth IRA that is completely tax-free — even under the SECURE Act's 10-year distribution rule.

Without conversions, those heirs would owe ordinary income tax on every dollar withdrawn from the inherited traditional IRA, potentially at 32% or higher if they are working professionals during their peak earning years. The tax savings for heirs can easily exceed $200,000 to $400,000 on a $1.5 million inherited traditional IRA.

Key Roth inheritance rule: Inherited Roth IRAs are still subject to the 10-year distribution rule, but the distributions are tax-free. The 10-year clock starts the year after the original owner's death.

A revocable living trust is the foundational estate planning tool for FIRE households. It provides three critical benefits that matter more for early retirees than conventional retirees:

Every early retiree needs three healthcare documents executed before leaving their employer:

Once you cross the $1 million net worth threshold — common in the FIRE community — asset protection becomes essential. You have decades of retirement ahead during which a lawsuit, car accident judgment, or liability claim could threaten the wealth you worked so hard to build.

For FIRE households pursuing charitable giving, a donor-advised fund (DAF) allows you to front-load charitable deductions in high-income years (or Roth conversion years), reduce your taxable estate, and distribute grants to charities over time. A DAF contribution is irrevocable and immediately reduces your estate while giving you advisory control over future grants.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Do not wait until traditional retirement age to complete your estate plan. The moment you leave employer benefits, you need a fully executed will or trust, healthcare directives, powers of attorney, updated beneficiary designations, and umbrella insurance. Many FIRE retirees leave their jobs with $1 million or more in assets and no estate plan in place. Every day without these documents is a day your family is exposed to probate, court-appointed guardianship, and preventable tax consequences.

Absolutely. If you have any assets, dependents, or strong preferences about medical care, you need at least a will, healthcare directive, and power of attorney. If you have reached FI with $500,000 or more in assets, a revocable living trust adds significant value through probate avoidance and incapacity protection.

Most non-spouse beneficiaries must now withdraw the entire inherited IRA or 401(k) within 10 years of the original owner's death. This compressed timeline can push heirs into high tax brackets. Roth conversions during your lifetime eliminate this tax burden because inherited Roth IRA distributions are tax-free.

For most early retirees, transferring your primary residence to a revocable living trust makes sense. It avoids probate on the home, enables seamless management if you become incapacitated, and does not affect your mortgage, property tax, or homestead exemption in most states. Consult your estate attorney about your state's specific rules.

Umbrella insurance provides liability coverage above the limits of your auto and homeowners policies. A $1 million umbrella policy typically costs $200 to $300 per year and protects against lawsuits, car accident judgments, and liability claims that exceed your underlying policy limits. For FIRE households with significant assets, it is one of the most cost-effective forms of protection available.

Yes, and early retirement is often the best time to do them. With no employment income, your taxable income is low, allowing you to convert traditional IRA or 401(k) balances to Roth at the 10%, 12%, or 22% bracket. This is significantly cheaper than the 32% or 37% rate your heirs might pay on inherited traditional IRA distributions.

Review your estate plan every three years at minimum and immediately after any major life event: marriage, divorce, birth of a child, death of a beneficiary, significant change in net worth, or a move to a new state. Early retirees have a longer planning horizon, making regular updates even more important than for conventional retirees.

Estate planning for early retirees is not a modified version of conventional retirement planning — it is a fundamentally different discipline. You face a longer incapacity window, a bigger healthcare gap, more exposure to tax law changes, and decades of asset protection needs. The FIRE community excels at building wealth through savings rate optimization and investment discipline. Apply that same rigor to your estate plan: execute foundational documents before leaving your job, optimize beneficiary designations for the SECURE Act, pursue Roth conversions during low-income years, and protect your assets with umbrella insurance and trust structures. The wealth you built deserves a plan that survives as long as your retirement.

#9139. Soldier Designs Limited-Edition Hublot Timepieces in Latest Artist Collaboration

Swiss luxury watchmaker Hublot is expanding its roster of artist collaborations. Its latest partnership is with Soldier (born Leonard Iheagwam), a Nigerian-born, London-based visual artist, designer and skateboarder.

Soldier has created 50 timepieces for Hublot in black ceramic and black-plated titanium adorned with little toy sliders and a cross. They’re a recurring motif in the artist’s work, which he first debuted in 2024 with Angelica Mara Jopling of Incubator. The dial of the 42 mm chronograph features more toy soldiers inside the dial and bezel. The collaboration with Hublot has been two years in the making, with products starting at £22,900 ($30,303). Related Articles ARTnews, Art in America, and Hublot Host Dinner at New York Headquarters of KidSuper $160K Jean Arp Sculpture Stolen from Art Cologne Booth

“The collaboration came together really organically. I was invited to the Daniel Arsham collaboration preview in 2024 and at the time I had made a few paintings that needed a space to preview, Hublot let me do it in their London store, which led to them asking me to do create a London watch,” Soldier told ARTnews during a preview at the Hublot store on New Bond Street.

Soldier says the process of designing the timepiece was “the same” as painting, invoking Marcel Duchamp’s Fountain (1917), in the sense that that both objects are “ready-made.”

“A watch is already an object, which has thought behind it, and so the process is quite simple,” said Soldier. He first visited the brand’s Swiss headquarters to witness the watchmaking process. “Art and watches are not mass-produced items, there are actual engineers who work on creating such a piece,” he said, adding that he never wore a watch growing up. He now ears a Hublot, engraved with prhase, “artist proof.”

The toy soldiers in the watch and in Soldier’s artwork are a nod to the artist’s upbringing in Nigeria, and the cross symbolism links to his father, who is a reverend: “We didn’t really come from a lot of money, and growing up, I used to skateboard wearing camouflage clothing, so I had a lot of run-ins with the police and army because civilians weren’t allowed to wear camouflage because of the civil war.

He moved to England in 2019, and his work today draws deeply on his adolescence. His solo exhibition at Jopling, titled “When The Saints Go Marching,” featured paintings inspired by memories of the war, as well as more nostalgic scenes: religious iconography and portraits of his family.

Soldier teased that he’s working on a “big” show for 2028 without revealing the name of the institution. He called the secret upcoming show “very important” because within the Nigerian creative scene. From his perspective, there visual art hasn’t taken off to the same degree as the fashion industry, citing Lagos Fashion Week.

“I didn’t grow up thinking I could be a painter, neither could my parents. I’ve only been showing work for the past three years,” said Soldier, who now counts art world figures like Charlie Gosling, Lorenzo Amos and Robert Nava as friends.

#9138. ‘Secret’ Location of a Vandalized and Rescued Banksy Revealed

A Banksy mural with a checkered past has been located by sleuths at the British Broadcasting Service (BBC). The semi-anonymous artist painted the piece in 2018 on Scott Street Bridge in Hull, a port city in East Yorkshire, England. The BBC has discovered that it is being kept in storage in Norfolk, more than 120 miles away, and that its future is unknown.

The mural shows a young boy, apparently dressed for battle in a helmet and raising wooden sword with a pencil attacked to its tip. He cries out “draw the raised bridge!” as he seems to sit on a graffiti writer’s tag. The joke being that the work adorned a bridge set to be razed: It’s been closed to traffic since 1994 due to its poor condition, frozen in a raised position. Banksy also plays with the notion of the pen being mightier than the sword, attaching an actual writing implement to a mock weapon. Related Articles AI-Generated Mural Sparks Backlash in Banksy's Hometown of Bristol Three Public Artworks by Banksy Have Cost UK Taxpayers Almost $200,000

While Banksy does not typically explain his works, some saw a commentary on Brexit; the referendum took place in 2016, and Hull voted 68% to separate from the European Union. The piece was painted over in white by vandals but quickly saved by a fast-acting window cleaner who rushed to save it. Some saw irony in the fact that authorities in Hull, named the UK’s “city of culture” in 2017, failed to protect the piece.

According to a city filing, the Hull City Council said it would pay a company some £60,000 ($79,420) to move the 22-foot-wide mural to the city’s Trinity Market, where it would also build and install a display case for the piece. The city council has not replied to repeated BBC requests as to whether the contract was awarded.

“Nobody will tell us where this painting is and when it’s going to be put on display,” local councilor Rosie Nicola told the news network. “It’s wrong.”

The whereabouts of the sculpture were hinted at in 2025, during a meeting of a committee of the council, when Angela Blake, the city’s assistant director of major projects, was asked where the artwork was. “It’s a secret,” she replied. Chris Jackson, the council’s executive director for regeneration, added: “I’m not sure we’re allowed to say.”

Engineering firm Alan Wood and Partners secured a £900,000 ($1.2 million) contract to dismantle the bridge and preserve the artwork, notes the BBC.

The artist remained anonymous for years, with various rumors of his identity catching fire. In March, Reuters claimed to reveal his given name and backstory.

#9137. Newark Museum Is Latest Art Institution to Transfer Ownership of David Drake Vessel

The latest institution to transfer its ownership of a David Drake vessel in its collection is New Jersey’s Newark Museum of Art, which said on Thursday that the artist’s descendants were given possession of an 1852 jug.

Other museums have undertaken a similar measure, from the Museum of Fine Arts Boston to the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts. But the Newark Museum said in its release that, unlike past ownership transfers, this one was initiated by the institution, which reached out to Drake’s descendants, rather than the other way around. Related Articles Theaster Gates Returned a David Drake Jar to His Descendants--It's Now on View at a Virginia HBCU Pots By Enslaved Artist David Drake Returned to Family from Milwaukee Art Museum

Drake is now widely recognized for the stoneware jugs he produced during the 19th century in Edgefield, South Carolina. He was born into enslavement and achieved freedom sometime after the Civil War. The jugs, which memorably figured in a 2022 Metropolitan Museum of Art exhibition, sometimes bore written messages whose meaning has often been debated. One vessel by him topped ARTnews’s list of the best artworks about America earlier this year.

The Newark Museum work was inscribed with the date “March 14, 1852,” and was signed by Drake—under a version of his first name, Dave—along with the initials LM. Those initials reference Lewis Miles, on whose plantation Drake was enslaved. It is displayed galleries for 18th- and 19th-century American art, and will remain on view while the ownership is transferred.

Over the summer, the museum reached out to Drake’s descendants. A release said that now, “with full support of the board of trustees,” the jug’s ownership was given over to the family and subsequently repurchased.

Lisa Funderbunke, the Newark Museum’s director and CEO, said in a statement, “We are deeply grateful to David Drake’s descendants for their trust and partnership. Restoring ownership of this work is an important act of justice, one that is rooted in accountability, repair and healing, and reflects the values guiding NMOA’s next chapter. As the Museum enters a new era, we are honored to continue sharing Drake’s legacy with the public in partnership with his family.”

Yaba Barker, Drake’s fourth great-grandson, said in a statement, “For over 175 years, our ancestor’s vessels have carried stories and history that must be told. Thanks to this agreement, our family’s mission for Dave’s work to be accessible to the public, and for viewers to recognize us as Dave’s heirs and owners of his legacy, is being fulfilled by Newark Museum’s leadership, and we are so grateful.”

Though the Newark Museum did not report a price for repurchasing the jug, Eileen Kinsella reported in the Art Newspaper that the transaction will cost “around $135,000,” a figure that is considerably lower than Drake’s auction record.

#9136. Say What? 7 Tips to Unclog Your Blocked Ears

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home.

Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up!

Why are my ears clogged?

Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked:

  • Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage.
  • If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection.
  • Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side.
  • Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too.
  • Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure.

Best clogged ear remedies

1. Pop and unclog

The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes.

2. Swallow, yawn, or chew

The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow.

3. Ear drops

Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes.

Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful.

4. Warmth and gravity

To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily.

5. Hit the steam room

Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 

6. Take allergy medication

Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears.

Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort.

7. Rinse away the gunk

Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing.

When to see your doctor

Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention.

What not to do when you have clogged ears

  • Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. 
  • Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries.
  • Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion.
  • Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation.

Takeaway

Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies.

PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

From Pop-up Pirate to Screwball Scramble, the Japanese toymaker Tomy became synonymous with mechanical puzzle games in the 1980s, and it's still going strong. It's just announced its first rebrand in 20 years, and it's the company's most radical identity change yet.

Tomy will have a new name for those of us outside of Asia. It's also introduced a new unified logo for all markets, and the dramatically different look has caused a lot of surprise.

See our guides to the best laptops for graphic design and the best monitors for graphics artists if you need new tools for your own work.

Tomy will now be known as Takara Tomy everywhere, consolidating its global branding under the name it was already using in Asia. In all markets, the familiar white and blue wordmarks are being replaced by a new logo design that combines the name with a rather abstract-looking symbol with a teal-to-magenta gradient. The company calls its colours 'Quality Blue' and 'Quality Gradation'.

While the symbol looks inscrutable, the company says it's based on a fusion of the katakana characters for 'asobi', a term that can be translated as 'play', 'recreation' or 'amusement' (see the video below). So although the logo looks indecipherable, it's actually a literal representation of the brand's playful spirit,

That playfulness is apparent in the wordmark too, if you look closely. There are two Ts, and three As in the company name, but each one is rendered different. The first A has a slight downward curve on the crossbar, the second a slightly upward curve, and the last has serifs on the feet and apex. From a distance, the wordmark looks fairly uniform and reserved, but each letter has its own personality.

However, some people aren't sure that the icon works. Even in Japan, people seem to be struggling to decipher its meaning.

Sign up to Creative Bloq's daily newsletter, which brings you the latest news and inspiration from the worlds of art, design and technology.

"Is it the chip on a credit card," one person wonders on X. "It looks like a seafood processing company," someone else thinks.

Some are even suggesting that the company's announcement that the new identity will be rolled out on 1 April 2027 is a sign that the rebrand might be an extremely early April Fool's Day prank.

I'd say it actually looks like a Screwball Scramble.

Here's the company's video explainer, which shows how the design was formed.

Tomy is an abbreviation of the name of Eiichirō Tomiyama, who founded the company in 1924. The company merged with Takara, another Japanese toymaker, in 2006. That led to the last rebrand, under which the company adopted the Takara Tomy name in Asia.

In an explanation of the rebrand on its website, Takara Tomy says it's now transforming from a 'toy company' to a 'play company' and that it will adopt the motto "One Takaratomy" as it unifies its branding".

#9134. Christie’s Posts Highest Watch Total Ever and Sells Bulgari Pink Diamond for $14 M.

The luxury market continues to be a major area of growth for the auction houses. Christie’s is holding its luxury sales week in Geneva, its biggest such event for jewelry and watches, and while the house hasn’t released its final totals for the week, early returns appear promising.

On Monday, Christie’s reported that its Rare Watches sale, held at the Four Seasons Hotel des Bergues, generated $58.7 million on 218 lots with a 100 percent sell-through rate by lot. That’s more than double the equivalent sale in November 2025, which generated $27 million on 179 lots with a 99% sell-through rate. Related Articles As Art Week NYC Kicks Off, Galleries Have Millions of Dollars of Art to Sell--And No Shortage of Naras Only Known Handwritten Draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' Speech Could Top $10 M. at Christie's

Leading the sale was a trio of F.P. Journe Vagabondage I, II, and III watches in pink gold, which together brought in CHF 6.7 million ($8.2 million). Each one sold for well over its high estimate of CHF 800,000 ($976,000): the Vagabondage I went for CHF 2 million ($2.4 million), the Vagabondage II for CHF 2.2 million ($2.6 million), and the Vagabondage III for CHF 2.5 million ($3.1 million). The Vagabondage is a blue-chip watch by independent watchmaker F.P Journe, highly desired for its wandering digital display and produced in extremely limited numbers.

Christie’s Magnificent Jewels sale, meanwhile, generated $49.7 million on 112 lots. The top lot, a 24-carat Fancy Intense Pink emerald-cut diamond ring by Bulgari, sold for $14.8 million, squarely within its $12 million–$18 million estimate. That total fell well short of the $75 million achieved on 108 lots at the equivalent 2025 sale. That sale’s total, however, got a considerable boost from the Mellon Blue diamond, which accounted for $25.6 million of the take. Excluding the top lot from both sales reveals a slightly smaller but still significant decline: the remaining 111 lots this year brought in $34.9 million, down about 29 percent from the $49.4 million generated by the other 107 lots in 2025.

Still, one suspects that the auction house isn’t too worried. In July, Christie’s released its first-half totals for 2026, reporting that it posted its strongest six months 2021 with a overall total of $4.5 billion. Luxury sales, which includes watches and jewelry, were up 15 percent to $539 million.

Whether the second half of 2026 ends up as strong as Christie’s first half will ultimately depend on its marquee evening sales next week in New York, where some 850 artworks will hit the block and are expected to generate over $800 million. Luxury is on the rise, but for now, fine art is still king.

#9133. What Is ‘Fiber Training’—And Why Should You Be Doing It?

With the fibermaxxing fad encouraging people to prioritize this chronically neglected nutrient, one issue keeps coming up: the side effects. As important as hitting your daily fiber goal is, your body doesn’t always make doing so easy. Fiber is difficult for your digestive system to break down and has to be handed off to bacteria in the colon instead (which is kind of its point), so piling on too much too fast can result in a barrage of painful, awkward, or inconvenient digestive symptoms—bloating, gas, stomach cramps, the whole nine yards.

To be clear, GI distress isn’t a sign to abandon your pursuit of a higher-fiber diet. “Even with fiber becoming a growing trend, people still greatly underestimate its importance and, also, just how many ways it benefits the human body,” Desiree Nielsen, RD, a recipe developer with a focus on plant-based nutrition, tells SELF. You’re probably familiar with fiber’s ability to keep you full, stave off constipation, and support gut health, but it wears plenty of other hats too, like lowering “bad” LDL cholesterol and stabilizing your blood sugar (not to mention reducing your risk for a slew of diseases in the long run). In fact, overlooking fiber is one of the top nutrition mistakes people make, according to experts.

But if you feel apprehensive at the thought of fighting constant stomach discomfort in the process of working to correct a fiber deficiency, we don’t blame you. In fact, it’s a complaint that Lisa Ganjhu, DO, a gastroenterologist at NYU Langone Health, hears all the time at work: “I have a lot of patients that will say ‘I ate more fiber, and now I’m really bloated and crampy,’” she says. Thankfully, there’s a way to curtail those disagreeable side effects so you can (comfortably) continue your fiber journey: a strategy Nielsen calls fiber training. Here’s what that involves, and how to start developing those “muscles.”

Fiber training is exactly what it sounds like: training your body to handle fiber better. It’s all about “slow, consistent increases in fiber to help you build your tolerance…while minimizing the potential symptoms,” Nielsen says.

You can think of fiber training kind of like preparing for a race. “In much the same way that you wouldn’t go out and run a marathon tomorrow if you haven’t run a mile before,” you need to work your way up to a high-fiber diet, Nielsen says. Similarly, Dr. Ganjhu compares it to a weightlifting regimen. Rather than lifting 50-pound weights right off the bat, “you kind of have to adjust slowly,” she says. “You start off with 10. When that becomes easy, you go to 20, then you go to 30”—and so on.

Fiber training is especially critical if you’re constipated at the outset, as many people are, according to Nielsen. Even though fiber can help prevent and alleviate constipation, too much at once can actually make an existing issue worse by overwhelming your gut. “When you add a ton of fiber to an already backed-up system, it’s kind of like a bottleneck on the highway,” Nielsen says: If you try to shoehorn four lanes into one, you’re going to end up with a jam on your hands.

Now that you know fiber training entails steadily increasing your fiber intake, you’re probably wondering what that looks like on a more practical level. Before we share specifics, some context for how much fiber you actually need might be helpful. Per the federal Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, women should aim for 28 grams of fiber daily from ages 19 to 30, 25 grams of fiber daily from ages 31 to 50, and 22 grams of fiber daily starting at age 51, though some experts recommend even more—a helpful set of parameters if you’re not sure where to start.

While the ideal amount of fiber to add to your diet while fiber training can vary from person to person depending on health needs (like a constipation issue), most people are “looking at [adding] probably three to five grams at a time,” Nielsen says.

With that in mind, you’ll want to choose a food that has a fiber content in that ballpark—say, an apple (around four grams of fiber), a half-cup of chickpeas (around five grams of fiber), a tablespoon of chia seeds (around five grams of fiber), or two tablespoons of ground flax (around four grams of fiber)—and eat a serving every single day until you feel like your body has adjusted (read: you’re not experiencing any additional bloating, gas, or other GI side effects). This process typically takes around five to seven days, according to Nielsen, but everyone’s digestive system is different, so don’t worry if you need more (or less!) time. “It really is about listening to your body and individualizing the rate at which you increase,” Nielsen says. “You have to follow your symptoms and go slow,” Dr. Ganjhu agrees.

Then, you can tack on another dose—like a second apple, a full cup of chickpeas, two tablespoons of chia seeds, or four tablespoons of ground flax. Continue increasing your fiber intake in these increments (and at this pace) until you’ve hit your daily fiber goal. If you’re a 35-year-old woman starting from scratch, reaching 25 grams of fiber—the recommended daily amount for that age—would take around five five-gram doses, six four-gram doses, or eight three-gram doses, for example.

People who are constipated may want to specifically fiber train with foods that are low in FODMAPs—fermentable carbohydrates particularly hard on sensitive stomachs—according to Nielsen. Like we said above, increasing your fiber intake when you’re backed up can, well, backfire, so low-FODMAP foods are more likely to be a safe bet than their high-FODMAP counterparts. Kiwis, which contain four grams of fiber in a two-fruit serving, are an especially strong option if you fall into this category (and they’ve even been specifically studied as a dietary constipation treatment), Nielsen says. Similarly, she adds, a gentle fiber supplement like Metamucil, which is made from psyllium husk, also “provides a lot of the benefits, but tends to be less irritating to a troubled system.”

Another tip: If you’re constipated, make sure to drink plenty of water as well (though the oft-referenced eight-glasses-a-day requirement is something of a myth!). Because fiber needs water to work its stool-softening magic, insufficient fluids could leave your bowel movements hard and dry, exacerbating the problem.

Whatever new fiber sources you choose, taking this slow-and-steady approach should help ease the transition to a higher intake. “If you’re someone who doesn’t eat a lot of fiber and all of a sudden you start eating 30 grams of it, the colon is just not going to know how to manage that efficiently,” Dr. Ganjhu says. But by leveling up little by little? You can heighten that “colonic fitness”—and sidestep the worst of the awkward stage.

#9132. Are Tangerines Good for You? 5 Health Benefits You Might Love

Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

These tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:

Tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s new best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

But wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

Last medically reviewed on June 26, 2024

#9131. Chicago’s Viral ‘Bean’ Stunt Inspires Londoners to Move the Marble Arch

Londoners want to get in on the viral stunt of the Bean, British Indian artist Anish Kapoor’s silvery sculpture Cloud Gate (2006), by wanting to move the Marble Arch, designed by John Nash in 1827.

“Bean there, done that,” as Ocula reports, responding to a public listing on the platform Partiful planned for Saturday, inviting people to move the 19th-century white marble-faced triumphal arch 17.78 cm (7 inches) to the left, the same distance that Chicagoans recently tried to push Kapoor’s sculpture in the city’s Millennium Park. The Chicago stunt failed to work, primarily because the Bean, as the public artwork is nicknamed, weighs 110 tons. Related Articles In Viral Stunt, Hundreds Try and Fail to Move Anish Kapoor's 'Bean' Seven Inches to the Left, To Help the Man Supposedly Trapped Inside Anish Kapoor Says the US Should Be Barred from the Venice Biennale over Trump's 'Politics of Hate'

The event description on Partiful said, “We have been made aware that the top floor of the marble arch [sic] was used for incarceration. People could still be trapped inside.” A representative of the artist Stuart Semple, who is known for disputing with Anish Kapoor in the past over questions like paint color, told Ocula that Londoners supported Chicago bean-pushers. The representative added that “planning to push the Arch to send a clear message that the bloke in the Bean must be freed” and that “moving the Arch will prove to Chicago that it’s possible, and will hopefully inspire them to try again to free the man.”

The Bean-pushing phenomenon has been all fun and games on social media. The Instagram account @Maninabean on Monday said that “as a coalition of non-violent like-minded individuals, we commend all action towards freeing the man.” The Instagram account was created in 2025 with its first published post on July 28, 2025 with the caption of “HE IS IN THERE,” accompanied by a paper cutout of a man inside a bean.

#9130. Why Are People Taking CoQ10 Supplements for Longevity, and Do They Work?

Coenzyme Q10, or CoQ10, was once a niche supplement, known best in wellness circles for its possible benefits for heart health and fertility. But now the antioxidant’s star is rising for a new reason: its purported longevity-boosting powers.

The appeal of CoQ10 has grown as researchers have explored its effects on various conditions, with small studies revealing, for example, it may help boost insulin sensitivity, cut the frequency of migraine attacks, and alleviate muscle aches from statins used for high cholesterol. But as of late, there’s excitement around its broader anti-aging potential because of how it supports our mitochondria, which you may remember from high school biology as the “powerhouse of the cell.”

That role has punched CoQ10’s ticket into the longevity club, alongside other supplements thought to lend a hand to mitochondria (like urolithin A and nicotinamide mononucleotide, or NMN). There’s even a synthetic derivative of CoQ10 designed specifically for better absorption by mitochondria, which is called mitoquinone (or MitoQ), that’s gaining hype among celeb trainers and athletes for boosting energy, recovery, and “cellular health.”

But is CoQ10 all it’s cracked up to be when it comes to longevity? Read on to learn more before grabbing a bottle of this supplement.

Our cells naturally produce CoQ10, a molecule that acts like a conveyor belt for charged particles inside our mitochondria, enabling them to “efficiently create adenosine triphosphate, or ATP,” the “currency for cellular energy,” Anthony Molina, PhD, a professor of medicine at UC San Diego who studies aging biomarkers, tells SELF. That’s a big deal, as all cells rely on that energy to complete their daily functions. As we age, both the number and energy-producing powers of mitochondria drop off—a process involved in the development of many age-related diseases, Dr. Molina points out. Meanwhile, CoQ10 levels also decline with age, leading to the idea that we should take it in supplement form for better mitochondrial (and, in turn, overall) health.

Beyond its role in energy production, CoQ10 is also an antioxidant that is “very powerful in capturing free radicals,” or volatile molecules that can harm cells, Daria Mochly-Rosen, PhD, a professor of chemical and systems biology at Stanford University and coauthor of The Life Machines: How Taking Care of Your Mitochondria Can Transform Your Health, tells SELF. By stabilizing those molecules, CoQ10 may help to keep that damage (a.k.a. oxidative stress) from piling up and also contributing to aging and the development of chronic disease.

Separately, CoQ10 has potential benefits as it relates to cardiovascular health: It’s anti-inflammatory and may also improve the function of blood vessels, helping regulate blood pressure, JoAnn E. Manson, MD, DrPH, chief of the division of preventive medicine at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School, tells SELF. These upsides could lower risk for heart disease, the number-one killer in the US.

Despite the promising mechanisms above, “the evidence base just isn’t yet there,” Dr. Manson says. The studies we do have on CoQ10 and longevity are in mice and rats—and while a few suggest a lifespan-extending effect, or a way to reverse some cognitive decline once it starts, others show no anti-aging upsides in healthy animals. Besides, “we find again and again that humans are not just large, non-hairy mice,” Dr. Mochly-Rosen points out, “so we can’t assume the results transfer.”

Studies in people have been focused on CoQ10 as an intervention for specific diseases, particularly cardiovascular ones. All the experts say the strongest evidence for longevity is in those with heart failure, who have low CoQ10 levels—taking the supplement alongside standard treatment has been shown to reduce the need for hospitalization and risk of early death, possibly because of its mitochondrial perks.

But logistically, it’s a lot trickier to prove that CoQ10 prolongs life in healthy people versus in those with a medical condition or known CoQ10 deficiency. In the absence of these studies, it might be tempting to take a logical leap: If we know CoQ10 supports mitochondrial function, and levels of both dip with age and disease, supplementing with CoQ10 seems like it should help you live longer. But the problem is, we don’t know exactly what drives the mitochondrial issues that occur with age, Dr. Molina says. “So maybe you’re not taking a shot in the dark because we know that mitochondria has something to do with healthy aging, but using CoQ10 as the tool is like taking a shot in a dimly lit room,” he says. “It’s not clear whether you’re hitting the right target.”

As with any supplement, it’s best to ask your doctor before adding CoQ10 to your routine. While there’s a good deal of data to suggest it’s safe and well-tolerated, there are some people who shouldn’t take it, generally because of interactions with prescription drugs, Dr. Molina points out. The main concern is with blood thinners (a.k.a. anticoagulants) like warfarin (which are often prescribed after a blood clot)—CoQ10 could make these drugs less effective, Dr. Manson says. It’s also extra important to check in with your doctor first if you take insulin or are receiving treatment for cancer. Though CoQ10 doesn’t usually cause side effects, you could also wind up with some mild GI upset or insomnia, Dr. Manson adds.

There’s also the quality-control problem that comes with any supplement. These are not subjected to the same FDA regulations as medications are, meaning you can’t know for sure that you’re getting what the bottle promises. Studies of certain CoQ10 supplements have found that they contained less of the antioxidant than the amount listed on the label, Dr. Mochly-Rosen notes. Your best defense against winding up with a sugar pill is to find a product that’s been third-party verified, she says—look for the “NSF certified” or “USP verified” stamp.

#9129. American Novelist and Four Others to Stand Trial Over Sale of Gold Looted from Shipwreck

In a story that sounds ripped from the pages of a novel, an American novelist, her husband, and three French nationals are set to stand trial in France next May for their alleged involvement in the resale of gold bars looted from an 18th-century shipwreck decades ago.

Eleanor “Gay” Courter, 82, an author of best-selling fiction, nonfiction, and memoir; her husband, Philip Courter, 84, a film director; Yves Gladu, 79, a professional underwater photographer; his wife, Brigitte Gladu, 76; and his sister-in-law, Annette May Pesty, 80, have all been charged with conspiracy. Some also face charges of money laundering and receiving stolen goods. Related Articles Suspected Thieves Flee Dresden Museum Complex After Being Spotted by Security Guard Three Works of Sacred Art Stolen From Spanish Churches as Authorities Warn of Rise in Art Theft

According to her website, Gay Courter has mainly written historical fiction and thrillers. And in case you were wondering, none of her books has a plot involving gold looted from a mysterious shipwreck.

The case will go before a criminal court in Brest on May 27, 2027, Agence France-Presse reported.

The case begins with the 1974 discovery of Le Prince de Conty, a French trading ship that sank off the coast of Brittany in 1746. The wreck was found 30 to 50 feet underwater near the island of Belle-Île-en-Mer. After gold bullion was discovered there, the site was looted in 1975. Lawsuits tied up the wreck until the mid-1980s, according to France’s Department of Underwater Archaeological Research (DRASSM). In 1985, archaeologists resumed excavations to the site and recovered Chinese porcelain dating to the 18th century, tea crates, and three ingots of Chinese gold. However that same year, a storm battered the ship and the wreck was reburied.

The current investigation began in 2018, when Michel L’Hour, then-director of DRASSM, reported a suspicious sale of five gold ingots on the website of a US auction house. L’Hour told US officials he believed the ingots came from Le Prince de Conty. The objects were seized and returned to France in 2022.

Investigators identified Gay Courter as the seller of the ingots. She said Pesty and Pesty’s late partner, Gérard, had given her the gold. Pesty, for her part, had appeared with the gold on Antiques Roadshow in 1999 and said she found it while diving near Cape Verde. Investigators found that story implausible and turned their attention to Yves Gladu.

In 2022, while in custody, Gladu confessed to looting 16 gold bars from Le Prince de Conty over 40 dives to the site between 1976 and 1999. He said he had sold the gold in 2006 to a retired military officer living in Switzerland, and he denied any connection to the Courters. Investigators found, however, that Gladu had known the Courters since the 1980s and had vacationed with them three times.

The Courters were detained in 2022 and placed under house arrest. Investigators found that the couple had at one point held at least 23 gold bars and had sold 18 of them for nearly $200,000. The Courters say the money was meant to go to Gladu. Last year, their lawyer, Grégory Lévy, told the Guardian that the couple had no idea the gold was looted and “didn’t see the harm as in the United States regulations for gold are completely different from those in France.” He said they did not profit from the sales.

Earlier this week, Lévy told AFP that he will argue for the Courters’ acquittal. The Gladus declined to comment to AFP on the trial.

#9128. Everyone Wants This Unapproved Weight Loss Drug—And Some Have Found a Way to Get It

For all the hype surrounding GLP-1 weight loss medications like Wegovy and Zepbound, these drugs don’t work for everyone. Nearly 17% of people on these medications are considered “non-responders,” leaving them looking for a different solution. But there’s a buzzy new medication waiting in the wings. While it’s not yet approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), people are already seeking it out.

It’s called retatrutide, and it’s a triple-agonist medication, which means it acts on three different receptors in the body. By comparison, Wegovy (semaglutide) acts on one receptor, while Zepbound (tirzepatide) works on two.

Retatrutide is already being hailed as a game changer in an area of health that’s already welcomed plenty of impressive medications in the past few years. In fact, clinical trial results show that it’s so effective for weight loss that some people have dropped out of the trials because they felt that they lost too much weight.

But retatrutide is still being tested in clinical trials. Eli Lilly, which makes reatrutide and Zepbound, hasn’t even submitted the trial results yet to the FDA for approval. So this is still an experimental medication—and versions of it are being sold online for cheap.

Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, California, tells SELF that retatrutide is “not really available” for use just yet, short of signing up for a clinical trial. There is no set timeline for when it will hit the market, given that clinical trial results have not yet been submitted to the FDA.

If you’ve struggled with losing weight on a GLP-1 medication or just want to pay significantly less for what appears to be the next big thing in weight loss drugs, it’s understandable to be tempted to add this to your cart. Here’s why doctors recommend resisting the urge.

Retatrutide is similar to GLP-1 medications in a few ways. Namely, it’s used for weight loss and is given once a week through an injection. Like Wegovy, Ozempic, and Zepbound, retatrutide works by reducing appetite and slowing digestion.

But retatrutide has more going on than that. This medication acts on three hormone receptors in the body—glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP), and glucagon (GCG). “This is the first one in the pipeline to work on three different receptors,” says Dr. Ali. “The theory is that the more receptors it affects, the more effective the drug will be.”

The medication is currently in phase-three clinical trials, and it’s had some impressive results that suggest it could be the most effective drug for weight loss yet. The latest clinical trial results show that participants lost an average of 28.7% of their body weight on the highest dose of retatrutide over 68 weeks. By comparison, tirzepatide users lost an average of 15% to 22.5% over 72 weeks during clinical trials, and semaglutide users lost 10% to 15% of their body weight over 68 weeks during clinical trials.

It takes a little detective work, but there are some pharmacies that are selling the drug online.

In fact, this has become such an issue that the FDA issued a press release in early February, stressing that it’s illegal to sell retatrutide (and fellow experimental weight loss medication cagrilintide) right now. That includes picking up the medication from a compounding pharmacy.

“Retatrutide and cagrilintide cannot be used in compounding under federal law,” the release states. “Additionally, these are not components of FDA-approved drugs and have not been found safe and effective for any condition.”

The FDA also noted that its officials have issued warning letters to companies that are distributing these medications.

This is hardly shocking, but doctors really want you to take a pass on using retatrutide before it’s FDA-approved.

“People should wait to take medications until they are approved by the FDA to maximize safety,” Richard Siegel, MD, codirector of the Diabetes and Lipid Center at Tufts Medical Center and endocrinologist at Tufts Medicine Weight & Wellness Center–Stoneham, tells SELF. “All scientific data in animals initially and then humans are carefully reviewed by the FDA for any signals that a medication may be harmful.”

That includes side effects you might experience now or in the future, Dr. Ali points out. Compounding pharmacies have become a gray area. They’re able to legally produce and sell their own versions of popular medications when the FDA-approved versions are in shortage. But technically this is no longer legal once the medications are out of shortage.

But compounded drugs aren’t carefully regulated and may not even have the same ingredients or concentration as the medication they’re designed to mimic, Dr. Siegel says. “While these medications may be safe, there is less oversight in their production,” he says.

Dr. Ali warns against going directly through a compounding pharmacy, noting that it’s safer to work with your health care provider if you plan to go this route. “The worst-case scenario is that you’re getting something unsafe or ineffective,” he says.

But, with all medications, Dr. Ali says it’s best to use the FDA-approved version whenever possible. “It’s going to work in a predictable way, and the side effect profile will be well-studied,” he says.

Dr. Siegel points out that there are a lot of options to lose weight right now. And, if you haven’t had success on one, he recommends talking to your healthcare provider about trying a different medication or strategy. If you haven’t had luck while working with a primary care physician, Dr. Ali suggests seeing an obesity medicine specialist who will be more knowledgeable about treatment options.

“Medications for weight management are a powerful tool that should be used together with a comprehensive lifestyle plan focusing on self-monitoring, optimal nutrition, and an exercise prescription, including both aerobic and resistance components,” Dr. Siegel says. Meaning, people who have the best results do more than take medication—they also focus on nutrition and exercise.

If you’re interested in taking a weight loss medication or your existing treatment isn’t working, talk to a healthcare provider who specializes in this area. “These medications are designed for people with significant weight to lose,” Dr. Ali says. “Most likely, they will need to be taken long-term.” That makes getting a well-vetted medication from a reputable source even more important, he points out.
